gitCommit.subject: One budget per agent, in the agent's Settings: API providers and coding CLIs counted together (#447) (#496)
gitCommit.body:
One budget per agent, in the agent's Settings: API providers and coding CLIs counted together (#447) (#496)

* Agent budget, engine: one budget per agent, every provider and coding CLI counted together (#447, part 1)

Quentin's decision (23/09): one budget per agent, provider-agnostic. Before,
the only field bounded coding-CLI runs (cli_daily_budget_usd, default 10);
max_tokens_per_job and the whole agent_budgets table were read by nothing.

- Migration 0127: agents.budget_daily_usd, budget_monthly_usd (0 = none),
  budget_alert_pct (80). The CLI cap becomes the daily ceiling ONLY where it
  applied (CLI runtime or code-task tool attached), so no agent gains a
  ceiling it never had. cli_daily_budget_usd, max_tokens_per_job and
  agent_budgets are dropped. Idempotent; real-Postgres test replays the fold.
- packages/db readAgentSpend / readAgentBudgetState: llm_calls + cli_runs of
  the agent, windows at midnight and on the 1st in the WORKSPACE timezone.
  One counter for the runner, the CLI guard and the screen.
- assertAgentBudget (was assertCliBudget) refuses a CLI run when the agent is
  over a ceiling. Codex is no longer exempt: the budget is the agent's.
- The job loop reads the budget at the top of every turn and stops with
  agent_budget_exceeded, delivering what the run wrote (the #442 stop point).

Tests: counter (providers, NULL costs, other agents, fixed-date windows in
three timezones), CLI guard (day, month, API calls counted, 0 = none),
runner (stop before any call with the exact line; under budget runs),
migration. Mutations on the runner check and the CLI guard go red.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01P8rFhmuaG6P1eEdUpre4a7

* Agent budget, screen: the agent's Settings tab gets a Budget section; the CLI cards lose their own field (#447, part 2)

- Settings, Budget: what the agent spent today and this month (the same
  counter the runner applies), daily and monthly ceilings, the warning share.
  The status says "N% of the daily ceiling spent" from the warning share, and
  the pause once a ceiling is reached ("runs stop until midnight").
- get/setAgentBudgetAction (owner gate outside local-trust, bounds shared
  with the database CHECKs). setCliDailyBudgetAction and
  getCliUsageTodayAction are removed with their two fields: the coding CLI
  cards say where the budget lives and whether their harness counts in it.
- Docs: coding guide, operate, troubleshooting (agent_budget_exceeded).

Tests: section (spend, warning, pause, payload, bounds), copy, actions read
back from the database (sum of API calls and CLI runs, bounds, non-owner,
other workspace), e2e setting a ceiling and reading warning then pause.
Mutations on the warning, on the payload and on the card's note go red.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01P8rFhmuaG6P1eEdUpre4a7

* Agent budget: a stored timezone that is not a real one no longer breaks every budget check; 0127 says Codex agents gain a ceiling (review of PR #496)

- readAgentBudgetState validates the workspace timezone before use (same rule
  as resolveTimezone in shared): an invalid stored string made AT TIME ZONE
  throw on every read, so every turn and every CLI run of the workspace
  failed on a database error instead of a budget verdict.
- 0127's header said the fold changed nobody's behaviour. It does for agents
  on the Codex runtime: the old guard exempted them, so their 10 $ cap bounded
  nothing, and it is now active. The comment says so. Comment only: drizzle
  applies a migration by its timestamp, so an already applied 0127 is not
  touched.
- The spend query says why it filters by agent only (a unique id;
  llm_calls.entity_id can be NULL).

Mutation: the timezone validation goes red.
